A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIC-VLA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original DynaNav simulations, Unitree Go2 robot experiments, and component and latency ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds baseline comparisons, prediction-horizon and controller-depth ablations, and odometry-drift experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix D revises the stated inference procedure in Algorithms 3–4: v2 computes latency and motion offsets from metadata attached to the completed KV cache inside predict_async, replacing external generation-history bookkeeping, and explicitly passes them to the policy. The backbone, architecture, losses, and training stages remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation rerun.

E1.justification: Training datasets, four DynaNav environments, and four physical navigation tasks are retained. V2 adds navigation under accumulated translation and rotation measurement noise, extending evaluation to a distinct noisy-input condition without adding datasets or domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated OmniVLA and MobileVLA baselines, with the latter described as MobileVLA-R1 in Section 4.1. This materially broadens the language-guided comparison beyond Uni-NaVid, NaVILA, and DualVLN to additional navigation VLA alternatives. Existing point-goal and real-world comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 changes the main-text success threshold from 1 m to 1.5 m, matching v1's appendix, and corrects the appendix learning-rate assignments to match the existing main text. New experiments vary prediction horizon, controller depth, and accumulated Gaussian odometry noise. These are bounded protocol additions and reporting corrections; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds sensitivity analyses for 1/3/5-second prediction horizons, 3/6/12-layer action experts, and moderate versus severe odometry drift (Tables 5, 13, and 14). These substantially extend validation of design choices and robustness to inaccurate motion estimates. The ego-motion ablation is retained unchanged, moving from v1 Appendix Table 9 to v2 main-text Table 6.

E5.justification: Both versions specify fixed-seed simulation evaluation and five trials per real-world task. Neither introduces confidence intervals, variability across seeds, or significance tests. Gaussian noise in the added drift experiment is an input perturbation, not a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result entries for the new comparators and three sensitivity studies. Table 1 reports SR 31.76 for OmniVLA and 32.94 for MobileVLA. Table 14 reports SR 55.29 under both no and typical drift, falling to 43.53 under severe drift. Matched pre-existing tables and Figure 5 retain their numerical values; the additions do not show improved same-setting TIC-VLA performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, latency definitions, and existing equations retain their substance. V2 explicitly writes the standard autoregressive cross-entropy loss already specified in v1; this adds explanation rather than a new objective, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain their meaning: a delayed semantic-control interface, latency-consistent training, and DynaNav evaluation demonstrating robust navigation. V2 clarifies the distinction from asynchronous architectures and supplies additional evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the incorrect statement that reasoning improves all metrics with acknowledgement of its higher collision rate, attributing the non-reasoning variant's lower rate to reduced activity. It adds interpretations of the new sensitivity tests and explicitly identifies runtime optimization and limited real-world evaluation as limitations. Extension to manipulation was already future work in v1.

D1.justification: V2 corrects the swapped learning-rate labels in v1 Table 6: v2 Table 8 assigns 2×10^-5 to the VLM and 2×10^-4 to the action expert, agreeing with both versions' main text. It also clarifies cache-metadata handling, explicitly identifies the ego-motion ablation as without RL, and documents distance-scaled Gaussian drift settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to VL-Nav by Du et al. and the robotics reinforcement-learning survey by Tang et al. Research positioning remains centered on explicitly handling delayed semantics. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or titles of existing works, including Vi-LAD/ViLAM.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to the introduction and experimental discussion, expands the loss explanation, corrects wording, and adds acknowledgements and an explicit limitations paragraph. The ego-motion discussion moves into Section 4.4. The main section sequence and most methodological and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5, 13, and 14, expands Table 1, and moves the ego-motion table into the main text. It corrects best-value emphasis for collision rate in Table 4 and rearranges floats and page layout. The twelve existing figures are retained, with limited label and caption edits.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through additional VLA comparisons and sensitivity tests, resolves conflicting threshold and learning-rate descriptions, and corrects the misleading all-metrics reasoning claim. Explicit limitations better qualify the deployment evidence. The explanation attributing lower collisions to inactivity remains untested, but the reporting corrections and added controls provide a clear incremental benefit. The central method, principal scores, and scale of physical evaluation remain largely unchanged.
